official.status_note: BME's admission page states that students can study at BME with a scholarship or as self-funded students by paying tuition fees, and offers an online application form for international students; no institutional scholarship with published award terms, amounts or deadlines could be found on the university's own pages.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarships page states that Hungarian State Scholarships cover tuition fees and help with living expenses for full training programmes, but these are government programmes administered outside the university.
benefits: Access to Hungarian government scholarship schemes listed by the university: the Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship, which offers no tuition fee, a monthly stipend of HUF 43,700 per month for BA/BSc, MA/MSc and one-tier master programmes and HUF 140,000 or HUF 180,000 per month for doctoral programmes, a dormitory place or contribution to accommodation costs, and supplementary medical insurance up to HUF 65,000 a year
The Hungarian Diaspora Scholarship for applicants from Hungarian diaspora communities
The Scholarship for Christian Young People programme founded by the Government of Hungary
The Students at Risk Programme for students who began their studies in Ukraine and want to earn a bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree in Hungary
Access to ERASMUS+ and EELISA funding once you are enrolled as a BME student
eligibility: You can study at BME with a scholarship or as a self-funded student by paying tuition fees
Scholarship eligibility is set by the relevant Hungarian state programmes rather than by the university
Applicants must have completed 18 years of age until the time of enrolment
Applicants must complete an electronic e-admission exam or placement test
requirements: Fill in the university's online application form at e-admission.bme.hu
Complete an electronic e-admission exam or placement test, with sample tests available
BSc applicants found to have inadequate skills in the basic subjects are directed to the one-year Preparatory Course before the BSc programmes
documents: High school certificate, or BSc certificate and transcripts for MSc applicants
Two recommendation letters for MSc applicants
Receipt of the transfer of a EUR 150 application fee
Description of subjects and transcripts of current studies for BSc or MSc transfers
selection_criteria: The university's scholarships page routes applicants to Hungarian state scholarship schemes and Tempus Public Foundation for terms and criteria
BSc applicants are placed according to the e-admission exam in Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry and English
coverage: Tuition fees and living expenses are covered by the Hungarian state scholarships the university lists, not by any BME-branded award

The Stipendium Hungaricum programme is described as offering no tuition fee, a monthly stipend, a dormitory place or additional accommodation contribution, and supplementary medical insurance up to HUF 65,000 a year
ERASMUS+ and EELISA funding are available only once you are already enrolled at BME
application_method: Apply for a government scholarship, usually the Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship, through the listed administrator Tempus Public Foundation at apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu, using BME as your host university
Or study at BME as a self-funded, fee-paying student through the online application form at e-admission.bme.hu
For preparatory and general courses, upload the CV, passport copy, high school certificate, English proof and the EUR 150 application fee receipt
For MSc programmes, also upload the BSc certificate, transcripts and two recommendation letters
BME requires a recommendation letter from your faculty if you are already enrolled there and want to apply for the scholarship
official.application_route: For university admission, use the online application at e-admission.bme.hu; for scholarship funding, apply through the listed Hungarian state schemes such as Stipendium Hungaricum, managed by Tempus Public Foundation.
official.study_mode: Full-time degree programmes; part-time programmes for fee-paying students are offered as semester abroad through the university's continuing education route
official.citizenship_residency: Open to students from abroad; the university describes its degrees for fee-paying students and lists state scholarships for foreign students
official.international_eligibility: Yes, via Hungarian state schemes such as Stipendium Hungaricum, Hungarian Diaspora, Scholarship for Christian Young People and Students at Risk
official.description: Budapest University of Technology and Economics publishes a scholarships page for incoming international students, but the page does not describe any scholarship administered by the university itself. Instead it directs applicants to Hungarian state scholarship programmes administered by the Tempus Public Foundation and related agencies: the Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship, the Hungarian Diaspora Scholarship, the Scholarship for Christian Young People and the Students at Risk Programme. The university's separate scholarships page under International covers opportunities for BME students to study abroad. Its admission page sets out the self-funded route with its own application documents and fee.
official.program_type: No inbound BME scholarship programme; the university routes incoming international students to Hungarian state scholarships
official.english_requirement: Applicants must submit proof of English language proficiency with the application; specific levels are set per programme and are not published on the scholarships page read.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no BME scholarship to apply for. The university's own pages route incoming international students to Hungarian state schemes administered by the Tempus Public Foundation, chiefly Stipendium Hungaricum, which covers tuition plus a monthly stipend of HUF 43,700 at bachelor's, master's and one-tier master level. So the decision to make first is whether you can secure Stipendium Hungaricum, which requires a sending partner nomination from your country, because your fallback is the self-funded route through BME's online application portal. That portal carries real costs of its own: a EUR 150 application fee receipt must be uploaded with your documents, and every applicant also has to pass BME's electronic e-admission exam, with BSc applicants who fall short in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry or English directed into a one-year preparatory course instead.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International applicants who already hold, or can realistically obtain, Stipendium Hungaricum status and want to study engineering or economics at a technical university in Budapest.
application_readiness_checklist: Decide early between the Stipendium Hungaricum route and the self-funded fee-paying route, since the document sets differ
For the scholarship route, use apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu and name BME as host university, then secure your sending partner's nomination
If you are already enrolled at BME and want the scholarship, request a recommendation letter from your faculty first
For direct admission, complete the online form at e-admission.bme.hu with the EUR 150 application fee transfer receipt attached
Prepare for the electronic e-admission exam, using the sample tests on the portal
For MSc entry, obtain two recommendation letters in addition to the BSc certificate and transcripts
common_rejection_risks: Submitting without the EUR 150 application fee transfer receipt, which is an explicit upload requirement
Assuming BME itself awards scholarships, when its pages only list state schemes
Being placed into the one-year preparatory course after a weak e-admission result in the basic subjects
Thinking transfer into a BME Stipendium Hungaricum place is open at any time, since the university has run it only in fixed windows
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: On the self-funded route, the full tuition fee for your programme at a Hungarian public technical university, plus rent and living costs in Budapest, and the EUR 150 application fee; the Stipendium Hungaricum route also leaves a shortfall because its provisions are described as a contribution only.
document_audit: BSc, OTM and preparatory applicants need a CV, passport copy, high school certificate, English proof and the fee receipt; MSc applicants add a BSc certificate, transcripts and two recommendation letters
Keep the fee transfer receipt as a separate upload, not embedded in another document
MSc transfer applicants must also provide a description of subjects and transcripts of their current studies
alerts: BME's International > Scholarships page describes study-abroad opportunities at partner universities, not inbound funding, so check the address carefully
The university describes its state-scholarship partners as Tempus Public Foundation and Hungary Helps, so terms change with those programmes rather than with BME
ERASMUS+ and EELISA funding at BME are for students already enrolled there, not for incoming applicants
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through the online portal with the required documents and the EUR 150 application fee receipt, sit the electronic e-admission exam, and in parallel pursue Stipendium Hungaricum if you need a scholarship, using BME as your host university.
